findings.title: Website is not reachable over HTTPS
findings.explanation: The site refused the connection when trying to load it over HTTPS, and the TLS check also timed out. This means visitors cannot reach the website at all right now.
findings.recommendation: Check that the web server process is running and listening on the correct ports, and verify firewall/security group rules aren't blocking traffic.

findings.title: TLS certificate status could not be checked
findings.explanation: Because the server isn't responding, we couldn't verify whether the SSL/TLS certificate is valid or expiring soon. This is a blind spot until the site is back online.
findings.recommendation: Once the server is restored, re-run a TLS check to confirm the certificate is valid and not close to expiry.

findings.title: DNS is resolving correctly despite the outage
findings.explanation: The domain's DNS records are set up properly and point to an IP address, so the problem is with the server itself, not with domain name lookup.
findings.recommendation: No action needed for DNS; focus troubleshooting on the web/application server.

findings.title: No SPF or DMARC email authentication records found
findings.explanation: The domain has no SPF or DMARC TXT records. Without these, it's easier for attackers to send fake emails that appear to come from this domain (phishing/spoofing).
findings.recommendation: Add SPF and DMARC TXT records for the domain, even if it doesn't send mail directly, to prevent spoofing.
